notes: OpenRouter facts for Meta Muse Wonder read 2026-10-13 (the day after release): model id, price, context, max output, modalities, effort levels and default, provider, throughput and uptime, plus the Design Arena rows OpenRouter embeds. The price equals the first-party price, so no pricing file is written for it (the Meta lane owns pricing/meta-api-2026-10.json). OpenRouter is a provider listing; only the Design Arena Elo rows are quality data, and they are an aggregator reading of Design Arena. Muse Wonder Full is not listed. Recheck on or after 2026-10-20.

claims.statement: OpenRouter lists Muse Wonder as 'meta/muse-wonder' (canonical slug 'meta/muse-wonder-20261012', display name 'Meta: Muse Wonder', created 2026-10-12 12:25 UTC) with one provider, Meta first-party (endpoint 'Meta | meta/muse-wonder-20261012', quantization unknown, moderated). Pricing: prompt $4 per M, completion $20 per M, cache read $0.2 per M, no cache-write price, web_search field 0.0025 (unit not stated in the record), discount 0 on the endpoint record. These equal the first-party price ($4.00 / $0.20 / $20.00 per M) and AA's figures; there is no OpenRouter markup and no long-prompt tier in the pricing record (Haiku 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Sol carry min_prompt_tokens overrides; Muse Wonder does not).
claims.implication: No separate OpenRouter pricing file is needed: it adds nothing to the first-party price except the confirmation that no tier override exists.

claims.statement: OpenRouter capability record for Muse Wonder: context 1,048,576 tokens; top-provider max completion tokens 943,718 (endpoint record 943,718); input modalities text, image, video, file, audio, output text ('text+image+file+audio+video->text'); reasoning is mandatory (cannot be disabled) with supported efforts max, xhigh, high, medium, low, minimal and default effort 'medium'; supported parameters include_reasoning, max_tokens, reasoning, reasoning_effort, repetition_penalty, response_format, structured_outputs, temperature, tool_choice, tools, top_k, top_p; tool choice none/auto/required/function supported; implicit caching not supported; knowledge cutoff not stated. For comparison on the same API: Muse Spark 1.3 has the same effort list and default 'medium'; Opus 5.5 default 'high'; Haiku 5.5, GPT-6.1 Sol and Opus 5.5 list max..low (no 'minimal').
claims.implication: On OpenRouter an unspecified effort runs at 'medium', not max. Every AA and Vals Muse Wonder run is max, so no board measures the OpenRouter default. 'minimal' is a Muse effort level with no benchmark row on any board read in this lane.

claims.statement: OpenRouter model page 2026-10-13: provider Meta, P50 throughput 67 tokens/s, P50 latency 2.68 s, 3-day uptime 99.93% (endpoint record: uptime last 1 day 99.93%, 5 min 100, 30 min 100; latency and throughput fields null in the endpoint JSON). Page-level numbers are OpenRouter's own request sampling one day after launch. AA's first-party measurement of Muse Wonder (max) is 104.1 tokens/s median output speed and 19.7 s median time to first chunk on long prompts (see the AA file).
claims.implication: Do not merge the two speed measurements (different request mixes and effort settings).

claims.statement: Muse Wonder Full is not on OpenRouter: the models API (461 models) has no 'meta/muse-wonder-full' entry and the page https://openrouter.ai/meta/muse-wonder-full renders an empty OpenRouter shell with no model content. This matches Meta's statement that Muse Wonder Full is available only by Muse Code subscription.
claims.implication: Consistent with subscription-only access; no API id or price exists for Full on OpenRouter.

claims.statement: OpenRouter embeds Design Arena rows for Muse Wonder (page label 'Muse Wonder (max)'): Models arena 3D Elo 1454 (rank 4), Code Categories 1370 (rank 2), Game Development 1387 (rank 4), UI Component 1384 (rank 2), Website 1358 (rank 2). Peer rows from the same API are in the score list; the peer labels on OpenRouter do not state an effort (Muse Spark 1.3 is labelled xhigh).
claims.implication: These are Design Arena Elo ratings embedded by OpenRouter, an aggregator; they measure generated UI and 3D artifacts by preference votes, not task success. Muse Wonder equals Opus 5.5 on UI Component (1384 each), is below it on 3D (1454 vs 1474), Game Development (1387 vs 1459) and Code Categories (1370 vs 1393), and above it on Website (1358 vs 1334).
